deities: Lord Shiva (Umamaheswara, presiding deity; Jyothirlingam in the sanctum)
Sri Vishnu (separate shrine with its own dwajasthambam)
Sree Valayanad Bhagavati (inside the Sree Krishna temple)
Narasimha Moorthy (small shrine south of the Vishnu temple)
festivals: Revathi Pattathanam (seven-day festival of scholars in the Malayalam month of Thulam, mid-October to mid-November)
Temple festival in the Malayalam month of Medam (flag hoisting in the Shiva and Krishna temples, concluding with Arattu)

history.dynasty: Zamorin (Samoothiri) of Calicut; now under the Malabar Devaswom Board with the Zamorin as managing trustee
history.period: Legendary origin at the end of Dvapara Yuga; structure rebuilt in the 11th century and expanded to its present form in the 14th century
history.summary: The Tali (Thali) Mahakshetram, a Shiva temple in the heart of Kozhikode at Palayam, is the ancient family temple of the Zamorins who ruled Calicut and one of the oldest temples in Kerala. Tradition holds that the Jyothirlingam in the sanctum was installed by Parasurama towards the end of Dvapara Yuga; the temple structure was built in the 11th century by Swami Thirumulpad and expanded to its present form under the Zamorins in the 14th century, reaching its zenith during their rule (the Zamorins bore the title Sailabdheswara). It was the venue of the Revathi Pattathanam, the annual assembly of scholars in Bharatha, Prabhakara and Vedanta Meemamsa and Vyakarana. Built in traditional Kerala style with laterite and wood, the two-storied sanctum is shaped like a chariot and adorned with murals of the Mahabharata and granite sculptures of Shiva's retinue. It is now administered by the Malabar Devaswom Board, with the Zamorin as managing trustee.

name: Thali Maha Temple
town_description: Kozhikode (Calicut) is a historic coastal city in northern Kerala on the Malabar Coast, famous as the medieval 'City of Spices' where Vasco da Gama landed in 1498. Once the capital of the Zamorin kingdom, it is known for its beaches (Kozhikode Beach, Beypore), the Mishkal Mosque, and a rich culinary heritage. The Tali Mahakshetram stands at its heart near the Palayam market, about 1 km east of the railway station.

travel.airport: Calicut International Airport, Karipur (approx. 23-27 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Kozhikode Railway Station (approx. 1-2 km); auto-rickshaws and city buses to Palayam.
travel.road: In the heart of Kozhikode city at Palayam, on Tali Road near the Zamorin's School (Chalappuram). Easily reached by city buses, autos and taxis; the temple is surrounded by the busy Palayam market.

visitor_information.best_time: October to May for pleasant weather; the Revathi Pattathanam season (Thulam, mid-October to mid-November) is the most culturally vibrant time. Early mornings are best for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning approx. 4:30 AM to 11:00 AM; evening approx. 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM (verify — one source lists 5:00 AM to 12:00 PM and 4:00 PM to 9:00 PM; festival days may differ). Entry is free. Strict dress code: men must wear a mundu (mundus available on rent); women should wear saree or salwar kameez. Only Hindus are admitted inside the sanctum area.
